# Exit codes

Every agentfs command terminates with one of these. A caller branches on the number rather than on the output, and a one-shot command repeats it inside its JSON envelope so a consumer reading a captured result reaches the same verdict as one that watched the process.

| Code | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | `ok` | The command succeeded and had nothing to report. |
| `1` | `findings` | The command ran to completion and reported findings. |
| `2` | `usage` | The invocation was malformed. |
| `3` | `path` | The workspace root could not be read. |
| `70` | `internal` | An unexpected fault ended the command, and the stack is reported. |
| `130` | `interrupted` | SIGINT ended the command. |

## Using them as a gate

`validate` separates "the workspace is conformant" from "the workspace could not be read", which is what lets it run unattended: a findings status is a result to act on, and a path status is a problem with the invocation.

```sh
agentfs validate ./workspace
case $? in
  0) echo "conformant" ;;
  1) echo "findings — see the diagnostics above" ;;
  2) echo "the invocation was malformed" ;;
  3) echo "the workspace could not be read" ;;
esac
```
